chapter_summary: She climbs to the scaffold after the lamps go dark and hears the ordinary world withdraw. The silence becomes both shelter and isolation.

spatality.place: a scaffold against a haveli wall, above a sleeping lane
spatality.season: dry season, the hour after the lamps go out
spatality.route: ground to the third rung and no higher
spatality.texture: cold bamboo, settling dust, one lamp left burning two houses away

poetic_parameters.movement: Language Poetry — word structure over clear meaning, used here to make silence audible.
writing_skills: abrupt line breaks where the breath refuses to finish
a single repeated noun standing in for the whole street
poetic_parameters.image_seed: the last lamp going out in a lane where no one has closed a shutter
poetic_parameters.volta: from relief at being unheard to the admission that no one is listening
poetic_parameters.sonic_texture: short flat vowels and the click of the final t in shut, night, quiet
poetic_parameters.line_gesture: short broken lines; the breath lands every third or fourth word and withholds
poetic_parameters.variety_note: Chapter one watched the wall in daylight; this poem is the first to stand above the ground and feel the town subtract itself.
poetic_parameters.metaphor_family: extinguished light, closed shutters, and the arithmetic of subtraction
poetic_parameters.address: the sleeping town, named but never woken
poetic_parameters.closing_move: one word repeated as a line, refusing to become a conclusion
